+TotallyNotASeaOtter "Some Games don't support Sli and Optimization is iffy.  A single Card solution is Always better."

This is the truth. SLI can be great when it scales well, but it can be a complete waste when it doesn't work at all. There are some best practices when developing, to help ensure better SLI scaling ("don't share data across frames" is a big one), but the issue mainly lies with whoever writes the drivers. In SLI and Crossfire, the multiple GPUs are treated as a single GPU. It's how the SLI/Crossfire drivers deal with parsing of data that determines how well the scaling is. You'll see tons of people yelling at game devs about SLI/Crossfire, but the onus is really on NVidia/AMD to optimize multicard support and develop profiles for various games.
